chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masrouq Al-Nahdi, from Musa ibn Umar ibn Bazie, who said:

I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! The people have reported that when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took to a road, he would return via another. So that is what he used to do.' He said, 'Yes, and I do it often, so do it.' Then he said to me, 'Indeed, it brings more sustenance for him.'

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you (a common honorific address to the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and material benefit of returning via a different path than the one taken?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Reza (AS) validates the Prophetic tradition of changing one's route to invoke divine blessing, explicitly linking this physical act to the spiritual principle of *tawakkul* (trust in God). He emphasizes that this practice is not merely a historical custom but a living Sunnah he personally observes frequently, promising that it serves as a means for increasing *rizq* (sustenance) through God's provision.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al haysam Bin Abu Masrouq Al Nahdy, from Musa Bin Umar Bin Bazie who said,

‘I said to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed you<sup>asws</sup>! The people are reporting that whenever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> took to a road, would return via another (path), so that is what he<sup>saww</sup> used to do’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And I<sup>asws</sup> (also) do it many a time, therefore do it’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘However, it is (upon, it brings in) more sustenance for him’.
